business_scope.primary_industry_name: AI Video Synthesis and Virtual Avatar Generation Software

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 249, as amended, including the transparency-register reforms effective November 1, 2021; formation and declaration under Part 2 (s. 5 et seq.); registered office and statutory records under ss. 9-10; annual reporting and register of individuals with significant control under Part 4; residual application of the Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348; the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 does not govern the limited partnership itself.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Corporate Online, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia, Victoria, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (prescribed form, filed as Form LP-1) submitted electronically through BC Corporate Online (bcregistryonline.gov.bc.ca)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow-account requirement under BC law; each limited partner must contribute cash or actual property (services are not an acceptable contribution) as specified in the partnership agreement, and the general partner must maintain contribution records sufficient to preserve limited-liability shield under the Limited Partnership Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Declaration of Limited Partnership annexed to these minutes is approved and shall be filed with the Registrar of Companies; the general partner is authorized to execute all ancillary instruments and pay all statutory fees. RESOLVED, that the Limited Partnership Agreement is adopted, the capital contributions of the subscribing limited partners are accepted, and the partnership records opened. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal agency for service of process shall be located at [registered address], British Columbia, and [name] is appointed registered-office manager. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed compliance officer for the transparency register and AI video-synthesis business operations. RESOLVED, that the partners are authorized to open bank accounts and to register with the Canada Revenue Agency and WorkSafeBC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation of Limited Partnership Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Corporate Online, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search or obtain a NUANS report to confirm availability; submit a Name Reservation Request through BC Corporate Online; the proposed name must include the designator 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' and must not be confusingly similar to any existing corporate, partnership, or trademark name registered in British Columbia.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (where not generated automatically by the online portal)
Identification of the requesting partner or authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the name, submit up to three alternative names under a new reservation request or file a written request for reconsideration within the response period stated in the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Corporate Online, Victoria, British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form LP-1 setting out the limited partnership name, general business purpose, registered office address (physical address within BC; no post-office box), principal place of business, full name and address of each general partner, and agent for service of process; pay the statutory filing fee online by credit card or registry account; alternatively, deliver the paper form by mail or courier with a certified cheque payable to the Minister of Finance; the limited partnership comes into existence on the date the Declaration is accepted and endorsed by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) duly executed by the general partner
Certificate of status or good standing for any corporate general partner
Notarized identification (passport) and proof of address for foreign partners, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or refusal, respond in writing within the stated cure period, correct the Declaration, and re-file; if the name is rejected, obtain a fresh name reservation; if entity records for a corporate general partner are deficient, supplement with certified corporate documentation or file a correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Partnership Governance Instruments and Transparency Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partnership (general partner and limited partners) acting through counsel; statutory records maintained at the registered office; Registrar notified of changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the limited partnership agreement; adopt the initial resolution approving the Declaration, capital contributions, registered office, and officer appointments; open the statutory records, namely the register of limited partners and the register of individuals with significant control in the prescribed form; appoint the designated individual responsible for maintenance of the transparency register; ensure any subsequent change to the registered office, general partner, or agent for service is filed with the Registrar within the statutory timeline; retain KYC documentation for each partner.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement duly executed by all partners
Initial resolution of the general partner and limited partners
Register of limited partners and register of individuals with significant control
KYC documents (passport, utility bill, corporate records) for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the transparency register or statutory records are challenged on audit, correct the entries within the statutory correction period (generally 30 days) and, where necessary, file a rectified record or amendment with the Registrar; counsel may issue a corrective resolution to ratify defective governance steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Federal and Provincial Registrations (CRA, WorkSafeBC, Municipal Licence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); WorkSafeBC; applicable municipal licensing authority (e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the CRA through Business Registration Online to obtain the 9-digit Business Number; register for GST/HST once taxable revenue exceeds the CAD 30,000 threshold or immediately if voluntary registration is desired; register as an employer and open a payroll account when hiring staff; register with WorkSafeBC under the Workers Compensation Act for occupational injury coverage before the first worker is engaged; obtain a municipal business licence for any physical office location; file the limited partnership annual report with BC Registries each year and maintain the transparency register filings.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the accepted Declaration of Limited Partnership
Partners' identification and business address details
Certificate of good standing for any corporate general partner
Lease confirmation or proof of physical business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the business-number application, respond to the review letter with a certified copy of the Declaration and the partnership agreement; WorkSafeBC coverage takes effect provisionally upon application pending final clearance; a refused municipal licence may be appealed to the applicable board of variance or municipal licensing commission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None at the federal or provincial level for ISIC 6201 software publishing; local municipal licensing departments (e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence Office) govern physical premises only
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - AI video-synthesis and virtual-avatar software publishing is not a licensed activity under Canadian federal or British Columbia provincial law; only a local municipal business licence under municipal bylaw is required if an office or commercial premises is occupied

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Assessment Office, Province of British Columbia; Impact Assessment Agency of Canada for federal projects
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based software development and cloud-hosted AI video generation involve no physical works and do not fall within a reviewable project class under the Environmental Assessment Act (SBC 2018) or the federal Impact Assessment Act (SC 2019, c. 28); no EIA registration or environmental assessment report is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to manufacturing or processing; office operations must comply with municipal sewer and solid-waste bylaws, the BC Recycling Regulation for electronic-waste disposal, and, only if on-site backup generators are installed, the air-emission and spill-reporting requirements under the Environmental Management Act (not anticipated for a pure SaaS operation)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification and occupancy permit per the BC Fire Code and applicable local government building bylaw for the office premises; structural load inspection for any on-premises GPU or server equipment; emergency-response plan per local emergency-program requirements; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance and workers' compensation registration once employees are engaged; all clearances are conditioned on a standard commercial lease inspection.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) govern banking and financial market infrastructure; FINTRAC administers AML/CTF and large transfer reporting; the Minister of Finance and the Investment Review Division of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) administer the Investment Canada Act for non-resident investment screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current account and capital account convertibility. There are no exchange control laws requiring conversion approvals, no restriction on remittance of dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, or partnership distributions to non-residents, and no quantity or fiscal barriers on currency conversion. The Canadian dollar is a free-floating currency. A British Columbia Limited Partnership is a pass-through entity; non-resident partners are subject to Canadian income tax in respect of Canadian-source income and to Part XIII withholding on certain payments, but no foreign exchange authorization is required. FATCA/CRS reporting and Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) registration are separate compliance obligations. Profit remittance via partnership distributions does not face capital controls; however, the bank may require a certificate of compliance from the CRA for distribution withholding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose export proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or foreign exchange repatriation timeline. Export receipts may be retained in any currency, in any OECD country, and invested freely. Canadian customs and trade data reporting may apply for goods, but for SaaS/AI video generation services (ISIC 6201) there are no tangible export declarations. FINTRAC reporting applies to electronic fund transfers of C$10,000 or more in a single transaction, whether inbound or outbound, but this is a reporting obligation of the financial institution, not a repatriation mandate.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for low-value operational collections and vendor payments; Low-Medium for primary treasury and capital escrow. Legal constraints: Canada does not provide an 'Electronic Money Institution' (EMI) license like the EEA; fintech accounts are offered by payment service providers regulated under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA, in force 2024). Such providers, including Stripe, Wise, and Payoneer, must be registered with the Bank of Canada, but they are not chartered banks and cannot accept deposits, issue credit, or originate FX swaps. Funds collected by these PSPs are held in trust at CDIC-insured chartered banks. A BC Limited Partnership may use a fintech EMI only for merchant settlement and low-value disbursements, never for capital injection escrow, legal reserve, or large trade settlements. For ISIC 6201 AI Avatar Video Generation software revenue, Stripe/Paddle are permissible as merchant rails, but the operative account must remain with a Schedule I Canadian bank to meet partnership capital and governance requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted for British Columbia LPs when all signatories and beneficial owners hold Canadian driving licenses or passports and pass biometric ID verification. If any general partner or significant beneficial owner is a non-resident, most Tier 1 Schedule I banks mandate at least one physical meeting at a Canadian branch, or in rare cases a notarized virtual KYC interview with statutory declarations and apostilled credentials. For foreign-owned LPs with no Canadian resident director, the bank will require (i) a physical interview of the general partner's authorized officer at the BC branch, (ii) a BC Business Registry search and filing, (iii) a solicitor's opinion on the authority of the signatories, and (iv) a proof of Canadian nexus (business address, contract, or employment). Pure digital onboarding without in-person step is not available for non-resident-controlled LPs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to multi-tiered corporate veil and limited partnership split
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully completed Beneficial Ownership Registry schedule under BC Societies Act (Form 3); corporate structure chart showing each partner, intermediate entities, and ultimate individual with government-issued ID; notarized partnership agreement excerpt naming capital contributors; signed trust deed (if any); attestation by the LP's compliance officer under PMLA/PCDAs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner located in a jurisdiction considered high-risk by FINTRAC/FATF
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of passports and proof of current address (utility bill, bank statement), enforcement of enhanced due diligence via LexisNexis/World-Check, source-of-funds declaration with supporting trail (e.g., audited financial statements, sale deed, settlement statement), and a legal memo demonstrating the partnership is bona fide and does not constitute a shell or mailbox entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital injection (e.g., > C$250,000) without pre-existing revenue or credit history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed capital contribution agreement and schedule of committed funds; LP bank statements from previous 12 months supporting the origin of funds; notarized board/general partner resolution authorizing the injection; formation documents including firm consent and BC incorporation certificate; detailed business plan and 24-month cash flow forecast; completed FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Report (if applicable) and CRS self-certification form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI video-generation revenue model raises red flags due to high cross-border variable recurring payments and refunds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform onboarding evidence: SaaS merchant agreement with Stripe/Paddle, PCI-DSS compliance, domain and cloud ownership; customer contractual templates (restriction on unlawful deepfakes, copyright compliance); technical AML risk assessment showing low-risk rating under ISIC 6201; historical transaction sample and refund policy; annual attestation of compliance with Canada's Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA) and Canadian Digital Charter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient Canadian physical presence or revenue nexus for a BC LP (substance concerns)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or virtual office contract in British Columbia with business registration at an active office, bank statements reflecting Canadian operating expenses, GST/HST registration confirmation, CRA payroll account (if applicable), and a detailed substance memorandum outlining the LP's management, bank signing authority, and day-to-day Canadian decision-making exercised via resident agents or employees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign LP or investor to the BC LP's Canadian bank account. The wire message must include the precise legal name of the partnership, account number, and a purpose code such as 'LOAN' (if intercompany debt), 'EQTI' (equity investment), or 'DIVI' (capital distribution offset). For Canadian regulatory purposes, a consistent purpose code and narrative of 'capital contribution' reduces compliance friction. FINTRAC requires electronic fund transfer reporting for any single incoming wire of C$10,000 or more; the bank will ask for supporting documentation including a capital contribution schedule, source of funds confirmation, and CRS/FATCA self-certification. Non-resident partners must ensure the capital is contributed to the partnership's Canadian account and not routed through a personal or unrelated corporate account to avoid anti-money laundering red flags. If the contribution exceeds C$50 million or represents an acquisition of control of a Canadian business, the Investment Canada Act net benefit review thresholds apply; but for a small AI video-gen LP, notification only is required above the enterprise value threshold (C$5 million in 2024 for non-trade-related investments). The bank may request a letter from a Canadian counsel confirming the investment is not suspicious, together with the partnership's capital account ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements (cloud computing, licensing, freelance developer fees, marketing) will clear through SWIFT MT103 for cross-border non-USD payments, and via Fedwire/ACH for US-dollar payments to US vendors. For larger trade settlements (e.g., platform infrastructure, sub-processors, media content licenses), a commercial letter of credit (LC) may be issued by the Canadian bank for irrevocable payment undertakings, but because the primary business is SaaS/AI video, straight SWIFT MT103 is the preferred rail. All outbound disbursements must be backed by an invoice and a statement of services; if the payment is for royalties or licensing, the payer must apply Part XIII withholding (25% under Canadian treaty, reduced to 15% allowing for treaty with US) and file T4s or NR4s. For disbursements to non-residents, the bank may require the CRA's 'NR status' and a signed Form NR301 or a waiver. On amounts exceeding C$10,000, FINTRAC EFT report is automatic. GST/HST must be accounted for on imported services as a reverse charge; the LP holds an operational account and must maintain 6+ years of records of the underlying cross-border transaction flows. No separate clearing rail (e.g., CHIPS or TARGET2) is needed for an LP that transacts in CAD/USD/EUR/GBP; the Canadian bank's correspondent network (often via Bank of New York Mellon, JPMorgan Chase, or Deutsche Bank) handles the settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on CAD/USD, CAD/CNY, or CAD/INR for non-convertible counterparties; available through Canadian Schedule I banks under ISDA/CSA, provided the underlying exposure is fully documented.

Deliverable foreign exchange forwards and FX swaps (including tom and spot-forward packages) with the LP's treasury bank; these are unrated products permitted for Canadian non-financial entities if entered into for hedging the partnership's actual currency exposure (services revenue or supplier costs).

Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) and interest rate swaps to manage long-term capital injections or intercompany loans; permitted under Canadian federal derivatives legislation and Ontario Derivatives Act, subject to bank counterparty credit approval and margin posting under ISDA.

Vanilla OTC currency options (call/put) with a tenor not exceeding 24 months, used exclusively to hedge anticipated SaaS invoice exposure; covered by the Canadian Financial Institutions Act and must be transacted under the bank's internal suitability and board-approved risk policy.
Exchange-traded FX futures (e.g., CME/ICE Canadian dollar contracts) and options on futures; permitted for corporate hedging and subject to clearing with an approved clearing broker.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Registry Services (BC Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of registration in BC; the annual filing period opens on the anniversary and closes on the 60th day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 late-fee surcharge if filed after the deadline; if the annual report remains unfiled for two consecutive years, the registrar may administratively strike the limited partnership from the register; written notices are issued before dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; if interests are held by non-residents, the T5013 return is due within 12 months of the fiscal year-end and non-resident schedules must accompany the return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500) under the Income Tax Act; partner allocable losses may be denied or restricted until the return is filed; no strike-off sanction applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under the BC Partnership Act for a BC limited partnership. A certified audit becomes legally mandatory only if (i) the LP is a reporting issuer under the BC Securities Act; (ii) a financial-services regulator applies to the LP; (iii) the partnership agreement, bank covenant, or investor-side subscription agreement triggers an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for any LP that is publicly accountable; otherwise ASPE. The partnership may elect tax-basis preparation for internal purposes, but audited or reviewed financial statements used for third parties are prepared under ASPE.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A BC limited partnership is not required to file an annual UBO confirmation or an annual significant-control register. The partnership must maintain a current register of partners showing each limited and general partner's legal name, address, contribution, and the date and manner of any transfer. On any transfer of an LP interest, the register is updated when the assignee is admitted; there is no annual re-file with the BC Registrar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute book for decisions of the general partner
Registered office record containing the partnership agreement and appointment documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220 - USD 550 (CAD 300 - CAD 750) per year for a BC registered office and corporate secretarial agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 - USD 18,000 (CAD 10,000 - CAD 24,000) for a Tier-1 review or audit of an AI SaaS limited partnership with no inventory and a straightforward capital structure
